findings.summary: The CLI checks HEAD rather than main by name.
findings.evidence: The tip passed to the check is `athena.git.head()`. In CI this is fine: checkout uses github.sha, which is main on push and the default branch on a schedule. A maintainer who runs the command locally on another branch would get that branch judged, and the help text does not say so.

summary: The change adds `athena check --attribution` and it does what the request asks. The check reads only the athena/records branch (the local branch, or origin/athena/records if that is all there is) and main's first-parent commits. It starts at the commit the earliest landing-intent expects as its base and does not judge that commit or anything before it. Each later commit counts as attributed only when a landing record names it as host_commit and the intent that landing cites has a matching head tree and expected base. A commit with a matching intent but no landing yet is pending for up to 15 minutes from the intent and fails after that. Any other commit fails as unattributed, and the report names its sha. The check also flags a records commit that is not a fast-forward, local and remote records refs that have diverged, a missing records branch, a branch with no intent, and records that do not parse. Nothing in it reads commit messages; one test proves a commit claiming a job in its message trailers is still reported unattributed. I ran the 11 attribution tests, the 14 records_branch tests and 4 binary tests; all passed. I also ran the help output and both flag combinations by hand: the conflicting combinations are rejected with exit code 2. The new CI job matches every item in criterion 7. I found two minor issues and nothing that blocks.
